sourceEvidence.title: Plant Manager
sourceEvidence.quote: Proven experience in power plant management, with a strong understanding of gas turbine and steam generator operations.

capture.text:
The Signal Hill power plant is strategically located in Wichita County, Texas, near the rapidly expanding Dallas/Fort Worth metropolitan area. This 77 MW electric power generation facility utilizes GE gas combustion turbines, along with associated heat recovery steam generators and an ABB steam generator. Signal Hill plays a critical role in supplying power to the ERCOT market during periods of peak demand and supply volatility. The facility was honored with the 2014 Certificate of Recognition by the City of Wichita Falls, Texas, for its outstanding achievements in environmental excellence, including pollution prevention, waste minimization, and water conservation.
We are seeking an experienced and dedicated Plant Manager to oversee the operations of the Signal Hill power plant. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in power plant management and a commitment to operational excellence, safety, and environmental stewardship. As Plant Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring the efficient and reliable operation of the facility, while maintaining compliance with all regulatory requirements.
Responsibilities:
Manage and oversee all aspects of plant operations, including safety, maintenance, production, and personnel management.
Ensure compliance with all environmental, health, and safety regulations, and promote a culture of safety and environmental responsibility.
Monitor plant performance and implement strategies to optimize efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness.
Coordinate with ERCOT and other stakeholders to ensure the plant meets market demands during peak periods and supply volatility.
Develop and manage the plant's budget, including forecasting and controlling operational costs.
Lead and mentor a team of Plant Technicians, fostering a collaborative and high-performance work environment.
Identify opportunities for continuous improvement in plant operations, maintenance practices, and environmental performance.
Maintain strong relationships with local authorities, regulatory agencies, and the community.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant power industry experience, such as experience as a Power Plant Manager or in a comparable power generation leadership role, in lieu of a degree.
Proven experience in power plant management, with a strong understanding of gas turbine and steam generator operations.
Comprehensive knowledge of ERCOT market operations and regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to manage and motivate a diverse team.
Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, and operational excellence.

Bring more to life.
Are you ready to accelerate your potential and make a real difference within life sciences, diagnostics and biotechnology?
At Cytiva, one of Danaher’s 15+ operating companies, our work saves lives—and we’re all united by a shared commitment to innovate for tangible impact.
You’ll thrive in a culture of belonging where you and your unique viewpoint matter. And by harnessing Danaher’s system of continuous improvement, you help turn ideas into impact – innovating at the speed of life.
Working at Cytiva means being at the forefront of providing new solutions to transform human health. Our incredible customers undertake life-saving activities ranging from fundamental biological research to developing innovative vaccines, new medicines, and cell and gene therapies.
At Cytiva you will be able to continuously improve yourself and us – working on challenges that truly matter with people that care for each other, our customers, and their patients. Take your next step to an altogether life-changing career.
Learn about the Danaher Business System which makes everything possible.
The Manufacturing Director is responsible for leading Direct Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, and Reliability Engineering across a large-scale Discovery & Medical manufacturing site. This role uses Danaher Business System (DBS) tools to standardize best-in-class manufacturing and engineering practices and deliver sustained improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
Focused on meeting Discovery & Medical customer expectations for quality, cost and delivery, the role drives Associate engagement, labor and overhead productivity, and effective deployment of people and reliable equipment. It leads Manufacturing Engineering and Reliability Engineering teams to select and implement technologies and processes that maximize availability, uptime and efficient manufacturing across Cytiva’s high-volume, high-variety, regulated manufacturing.
As part of the Senior Site Leadership Team, the role leads, coaches and mentors Manufacturing and Engineering teams, addressing critical performance gaps and delivering sustained improvements across Manufacturing and Operations KPIs in line with Danaher Core Value Drivers.
This position reports to the Operations Director and is part of the Manufacturing Operations team located in Cardiff, UK. This is an on-site role with up to 20% travel, as required.
What You Will Do
Lead site Manufacturing, Manufacturing Engineering, and Reliability Engineering teams across diverse regulated operations, including high-volume automated Medical Device lines, medium-volume semi-automated Laboratory Device manufacturing in regulated cleanroom environments, and complex process-driven Biology production.
Drive Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost through the disciplined adoption and deployment of DBS tools, including Daily Management, Standard Work, Value Stream Mapping, 5S, Total Productive Maintenance, and structured problem solving (PSP), using action plans and well-chosen Kaizen events to drive sustainable results.
Deliver sustained improvements in OTD, Past Due, yield, OEE, equipment availability, Labor Productivity and Overhead Productivity by improving flow, uptime, schedule adherence, maintenance effectiveness and manufacturing execution.
Partner with site-based EHS & Facilities, Supply Chain, Quality, and DBS leaders to identify critical performance gaps, lead Kaizen events, and execute breakthrough initiatives that improve customer value and operational performance.
Lead Manufacturing Engineering and Reliability Engineering teams to optimize process capability, equipment performance, technology deployment, validation readiness and lifecycle asset reliability across all manufacturing platforms.
Build strong cross-functional relationships with upstream suppliers, downstream supply chain partners and internal stakeholders to improve flow, reduce disruption, and increase responsiveness across the full value stream.
Develop, coach and engage manufacturing and engineering talent, strengthening leadership capability, DBS competency, associate engagement and succession depth across the site.
Who You Are
Master’s or bachelor’s degree in relevant Business, Manufacturing, Engineering or Science based discipline, or equivalent years of experience.
Significant progressive experience in complex site manufacturing and engineering leadership within a high-volume, lean-driven manufacturing environment, ideally in Life Sciences or a similar regulated industry with high levels of automation.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex problems, communicate issues, and propose solutions to external customers and internal team members.
Strong analytical, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate ideas clearly, build understanding, and strengthen problem solving and relationships across peers and leaders.
Ability to operate effectively in a multi-tasking, dynamic environment, while maintaining a forward-thinking and customer-first attitude.
Ability to energize, develop, build rapport, collaborate, and influence at all levels within an organization. Acts as an inspirational, approachable, and humble leader who builds trust and engagement.
Travel, Motor Vehicle Record & Physical/Environment Requirements
Ability to travel up to 20% of the time, including visits to manufacturing sites and business locations as required.
Ability to work in a variety of manufacturing, cleanroom, laboratory, biological production, and office environments.
It would be a plus if you also possess previous experience in:
Life Sciences, Biotechnology, Diagnostics, Medical Device, or Pharmaceutical manufacturing environments.
Leading large-scale operational transformations through Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Danaher Business System methodologies.
Developing manufacturing leadership talent and building robust succession pipelines within global organizations.

Join our winning team today. Together, we’ll accelerate the real-life impact of tomorrow’s science and technology. We partner with customers across the globe to help them solve their most complex challenges, architecting solutions that bring the power of science to life.

Description
Alvarez & Marsal Private Equity Performance Improvement
Director: Operations & Manufacturing
(OPEN TO ALL U.S. LOCATIONS)
About Alvarez & Marsal
Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 15,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.
The Team
A&M’s Private Equity Performance Improvement Services (PEPI) practice, with offices throughout the US, focuses on serving the middle market and large cap private equity firms who have engaged A&M to help improve operating results at their portfolio companies.
Our professionals are aligned with a PEPI service line to promote the development of deep functional skills & experiences and to maximize our ability to tailor solutions to solve our clients' business issues.
We bring a structured and disciplined approach to create and capture value. We provide private equity clients with a broad continuum of knowledge and tools for cost improvements, transformations, mergers, acquisitions, and carve-outs.
A&M’s Operations professionals assist our clients in analyzing manufacturing operations, supply chain and distribution channels, procurement, SG&A operations, and sales force effectiveness for potential value creation opportunities and help drive them during our client’s ownership. From our thorough fact-based analysis, we assess the state of operations, identify key risks to investment and quantify potential EBITDA improvement plans for the buyer and seller.
The PEPI Operations group is a growing business targeting high growth in the next two to four years. We offer excellent opportunities for career advancement and leadership skills. The leadership team is focused on providing development opportunities, training, and exposure to international business assignments.
How You Will Contribute
We are seeking individuals that can lead and deliver large, complex client engagements, working closely with PE leadership to identify, design, and implement creative business solutions for their portfolio companies. Directors frequently lead the following types of engagements:
Gain a comprehensive understanding of a target’s manufacturing and distribution operations-- organization design, production capacity, efficiency, quality, planning, warehousing and team capability
Evaluate the maintainability and operability of production facilities
Review current and historical data to understand efficiency & capacity, including equipment conditions, maintenance logs, spare parts and detailed production numbers
Provide shop floor insights by talking with employees and customers and reviewing all available data
Identify potential cost improvement opportunities through lean improvements, outsourcing or consolidation of facilities
Develop transformation plans to drive proposed changes and identify key risks and mitigation strategies
Implement and oversee the quality of deliverables and effectively manage the team and day-to-day relationships to ensure exceptional performance.
Qualifications
10-15 plus years of combined professional industry and consulting experience, with a minimum of 4 years specializing in manufacturing and/or distribution functions
Previous advisory experience from a top-tier strategy firm, leading specialist, niche advisory firm, or Big-4 consultancy REQUIRED
Travel-- This role requires significant client-site presence, with travel up to 80% of the time — generally Monday through Thursday or Friday, including overnight stays. Candidates should be comfortable with a consulting travel lifestyle.
Experience working for or with private equity sponsors and portfolio companies. Deep functional expertise in one of more of the following areas:
Supply Chain Operations
Manufacturing Operations, SI&OP
Footprint optimization, plant consolidation and product line transfer
Manufacturing strategy, CapEx planning, Manufacturing 4.0/IIoT
Lean, Six Sigma, TOC and Value Engineering
Demonstrated track record working with C-suite executives as well as private equity deal and operating partners
Excellent fact-gathering and analytical skills, including business process mapping and quantitative analysis
Specific experience designing and leading the execution of internally-focused and externally-focused change/communications strategy.
Excellent fact-gathering and analytical skills, including business process mapping and quantitative analysis
Previous strategy and change management experience.
MBA a plus
Your journey at A&M
We recognize that our people are the driving force behind our success, which is why we prioritize an employee experience that fosters each person’s unique professional and personal development. Our robust performance development process promotes continuous learning, rewards your contributions, and fosters a culture of meritocracy. With top-notch training and on-the-job learning opportunities, you can acquire new skills and advance your career.
We prioritize your well-being, providing benefits and resources to support you on your personal journey. Our people consistently highlight the growth opportunities, our unique, entrepreneurial culture, and the fun we have together as their favorite aspects of working at A&M. The possibilities are endless for high-performing and passionate professionals.
The salary range is $150,000--$225,000 annually, dependent on several variables including but not limited to education, experience, skills, and geography. In addition, A&M offers a discretionary bonus program which is based on a number of factors, including individual and firm performance. Please ask your recruiter for details.
Alvarez & Marsal recruits on an ongoing basis. Candidates are considered as they apply, until the opportunity is filled. Candidates are encouraged to apply expeditiously to any role(s) that they are qualified for and that are of interest to them.
Full-time Positions and Part-time Positions Over 30 hours

Additionally, employees are eligible for paid time off including vacation, personal days, seventy-two (72) hours of sick time (prorated for part time employees), ten federal holidays, one floating holiday, and parental leave. The amount of vacation and personal days available varies based on tenure and role type. Click here for more information regarding A&M’s benefits programs.

Company Description Suit Trans is a family-owned trucking company with decades of experience and a deep commitment to redefining how the industry works for professional drivers. The organization focuses on improving drivers’ overall lifestyle, offering more flexibility, more time at home, and stronger earning potential. Suit Trans emphasizes fair, honest, and straightforward policies, along with quality equipment and benefits that support drivers and their families. The company believes trucking is fundamentally about people and relationships, and aims to ensure that those who have been underserved in the past can build successful, sustainable careers. Suit Trans represents a better direction in trucking by putting drivers’ needs and voices at the center of its business.
Role Description The Director of Dedicated Operations is a full-time, on-site role based in Rainbow City, AL, responsible for leading and optimizing Suit Trans’s dedicated fleet operations. This role oversees daily dispatch and load planning, ensures on-time service for customers, and maintains routes that align with drivers’ lifestyle and income goals. The Director will manage operational staff, collaborate closely with drivers and customer partners, and monitor performance metrics such as safety, service, and cost efficiency. Key responsibilities include developing and refining operating procedures, resolving service issues, supporting equipment utilization and maintenance coordination, and driving continuous improvement across dedicated lanes. This individual will also participate in strategic planning, contribute to customer contract discussions, and help foster a culture of respect, transparency, and strong driver relationships.
Qualifications
Operations leadership skills, including experience managing dedicated or fleet operations, setting priorities, and overseeing day-to-day logistics activities.
Transportation and trucking industry knowledge, with familiarity in route planning, dispatch, freight management, and driver scheduling.
Strong communication and relationship-building abilities to collaborate effectively with drivers, internal teams, and customer partners.
Analytical and problem-solving skills to interpret performance data, improve processes, and resolve operational and service issues in a timely manner.
Experience developing and implementing fair, clear policies and procedures that support safety, efficiency, and driver satisfaction.
Demonstrated commitment to safety and compliance with relevant transportation regulations and company standards.
Proficiency with transportation management systems, routing tools, and common office software (e.g., spreadsheets, reporting tools).
Relevant supervisory or management experience in logistics, transportation, or operations; a bachelor’s degree in business, logistics, or a related field is preferred but equivalent experience will be considered.
Ability to work on-site in Rainbow City, AL, with a hands-on approach to supporting drivers and operational staff.

Description
Director of Manufacturing
Do you thrive on leading manufacturing teams to deliver quality products on schedule?
Are you passionate about Lean Manufacturing and developing high-performing leaders?
Does working for a family-centric company with deep roots appeal to you?
Do the values of stewardship, versatility, and family resonate strongly with you?
Do you find the improvement of people’s lives through stewardship of God-given resources inspiring?
Then Bedrock Truck Beds is right for you!
Department: Manufacturing / Operations | Primary Location: Shiner, Texas | Reports To: President
Director of Manufacturing Job Summary
The Director of Manufacturing is responsible for leading and optimizing manufacturing operations across the Shiner and Beeville facilities, overseeing flatbed production, the flatbed finishing line, and Manufacturing Engineering. This position is accountable for achieving production goals, improving operational efficiency, maintaining product quality, ensuring employee safety, controlling manufacturing costs, and delivering products on schedule.
The Director will lead manufacturing and engineering teams to establish consistent processes, improve product manufacturability, implement Lean Manufacturing principles, and drive continuous improvement across both facilities. This individual must be a hands-on, results-oriented leader with a strong background in metal fabrication, welding, assembly, finishing operations, manufacturing engineering, and multi-facility leadership.
Director of Manufacturing Responsibilities:
Manufacturing Operations and Production
Direct manufacturing operations at both Shiner and Beeville facilities.
Oversee flatbed fabrication, welding, assembly, finishing, and final inspection.
Manage the flatbed finishing line to ensure proper workflow, production capacity, quality, and on-time completion.
Establish production schedules and ensure manufacturing resources align with customer demand.
Balance workloads, staffing, equipment, and production capacity between facilities.
Standardize processes and best practices across both locations.
Eliminate bottlenecks, downtime, rework, and inefficient use of labor and materials.
Manufacturing Engineering Leadership
Direct and develop the Manufacturing Engineering team, establishing priorities, responsibilities, and performance expectations.
Ensure Manufacturing Engineering supports production objectives, quality, cost reduction, and capacity improvements.
Lead the development and implementation of standardized work instructions, process documentation, production layouts, and manufacturing methods.
Drive improvements in fabrication, welding, assembly, tooling, fixtures, automation, and finishing processes.
Partner with Design Engineering to improve design for manufacturability, simplify production, and reduce manufacturing costs.
Lead engineering projects that improve labor productivity, product consistency, throughput, and equipment utilization.
Evaluate and implement new manufacturing technologies, equipment, tooling, and automation.
Establish engineering standards and ensure successful implementation of process changes across both facilities.
Use data, time studies, and root-cause analysis to identify opportunities for measurable improvement.
Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement
Lead the implementation and ongoing development of Lean Manufacturing practices across both facilities.
Establish a culture of continuous improvement, waste elimination, and employee involvement.
Apply Lean tools such as 6S, standard work, value stream mapping, visual management, root-cause analysis, and Kaizen events.
Improve production flow, reduce work-in-process inventory, shorten lead times, and eliminate non-value-added activities.
Identify and address bottlenecks throughout fabrication, welding, assembly, and finishing.
Implement labor standards, cycle-time measurements, and productivity metrics where appropriate.
Train and coach manufacturing leaders and employees in Lean principles and problem-solving methods.
Track and verify improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and delivery performance.
Leadership and Workforce Development
Lead, coach, and develop managers, production supervisors, and Manufacturing Engineering personnel.
Establish clear expectations and accountability for performance across manufacturing and engineering.
Build a culture focused on safety, quality, teamwork, ownership, and continuous improvement.
Ensure adequate staffing, technical training, cross-training, and succession planning.
Develop capable leaders who can manage daily operations while driving consistent results.
Quality, Safety, and Compliance
Establish and maintain quality standards for flatbed manufacturing and finishing operations.
Reduce defects, scrap, rework, warranty claims, and customer complaints.
Ensure corrective actions address root causes and prevent recurring issues.
Maintain compliance with applicable OSHA requirements and environmental regulations.
Promote safe work practices in welding, cutting, grinding, material handling, finishing, and equipment operation.
Hold manufacturing and engineering leaders accountable for safety and quality performance.
Cost and Budget Management
Develop and manage manufacturing and Manufacturing Engineering budgets.
Monitor labor productivity, material usage, scrap, rework, overtime, and manufacturing cost per unit.
Lead cost-reduction initiatives without compromising safety or product quality.
Evaluate capital investments in equipment, tooling, automation, and facility improvements.
Partner with Purchasing and other departments to improve operating performance and reduce material cost.
Materials, Maintenance, and Supply Chain Coordination
Coordinate with Purchasing and Planning to ensure material availability.
Align production schedules with inventory, labor, equipment, and shipping capacity.
Ensure preventive maintenance supports equipment reliability and minimizes downtime.
Coordinate finished-product flow through shipping.
Performance Management and Reporting
Establish and maintain consistent KPIs for both facilities and Manufacturing Engineering.
Conduct regular reviews of safety, quality, production, delivery, cost, and engineering performance.
Report results, risks, and improvement initiatives to executive leadership.
Use data-driven decision-making to prioritize projects and measure results.
Ensure accountability for improvement initiatives and expected business outcomes.
All other duties as assigned by management.
Director of Manufacturing Skills and Competencies
Strong analytical, communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency with ERP systems, production reporting, and Microsoft Office or comparable tools.
Director of Manufacturing Qualifications
7–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in metal fabrication, welding, assembly, or industrial manufacturing.
Demonstrated experience implementing Lean Manufacturing principles and delivering measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and lead time.
Experience leading Manufacturing Engineering, production operations, and multiple manufacturing departments or facilities.
Strong understanding of fabrication, welding, assembly, finishing, production scheduling, and manufacturing processes.
Proven ability to improve manufacturing flow, eliminate waste, and increase labor productivity.
Experience with Lean tools such as 6S, Kaizen, value stream mapping, standard work, visual management, and root-cause analysis.
Experience leading and developing managers, production supervisors, manufacturing engineers, and hourly employees.
Strong understanding of manufacturing process development, tooling, fixtures, automation, and design for manufacturability.
Experience managing budgets, capital projects, production capacity, and manufacturing cost controls.
Ability to travel occasionally between Shiner and Beeville (approximately 90% Shiner / 10% Beeville).
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
Experience in truck equipment, commercial vehicle upfitting, agricultural equipment, or heavy metal fabrication.
Lean certification or formal Lean training, such as Lean Six Sigma, is a plus.
Physical Requirements
Work may involve walking and standing in manufacturing areas and using required personal protective equipment.
Work Environment
Manufacturing and office environments, with regular presence on production floors. Primary location is Shiner, with occasional visits to Beeville.

Health Insurance
Vision Insurance
Dental Insurance
401(k)
Paid Time Off
Profit Sharing
Counseling

Director, Engineering Enrichment Operations
Date:
Oct 16, 2026
Location:
Oak Ridge, TN, US
Company:
BWXT
Req ID:

At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com. Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.
Welcome to BWXT
We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.
Position Overview: Director of Engineering – Enrichment Operations
As the Director of Engineering for BWXT Enrichment Operations, you will lead the full engineering function responsible for delivering a production‑ready centrifuge product and a high‑precision, highly automated factory capability. You will oversee engineering strategy from early concept through prototype/pilot phases to full‑rate production, establishing core systems engineering and systems integration practices to ensure disciplined requirements management, interface control, verification/validation, and seamless subsystem integration. This role is pivotal in standing up a modern digital factory, enabling high‑volume production with aerospace‑grade quality and nuclear regulatory rigor.
Location
On-site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee
Your Day-to-Day as the Director of Engineering
Engineering Leadership & Organization
• Build, scale, and lead a multidisciplinary engineering organization spanning manufacturing, process, facilities, automation, industrialization, and precision systems.
• Serve as the technical authority for manufacturability, scalability, risk management, and readiness.
Systems Engineering (SE)
• Establish a modern systems engineering capability that includes requirements management, architecture development, interface control (ICDs), configuration management, verification and validation, and model-based systems engineering/digital thread practices.
• Define “Definition of Done” at each development gate and ensure complete, build-ready Product Readiness Packs (e.g., BOMs, routers, test plans).
Systems Integration (SI)
• Lead end‑to‑end integration of subsystems into the centrifuge product and supporting systems.
• Develop integration plans, lab capabilities, fixtures, and test regimes to validate subsystem and system-level performance.
• Collaborate with the CTO and ORNL Design Authority to align qualification evidence and change packages; support seamless integration with CMDF pilot builds and transfer to CMF industrialization.
Factory Design, Construction & Startup
• Lead design, build, and commissioning of a high‑precision manufacturing facility.
• Integrate automation, robotics, and digital factory systems to enable high throughput, traceability, and tightly controlled processes.
Manufacturing Excellence & DFx
• Deliver engineering solutions capable of automotive‑pace production with aerospace‑grade quality.
• Drive design for manufacturability, assembly, quality, cost, and industrialization (DFM/DFA/DFQ/DFC).
Quality, Safety & Compliance
• Ensure all engineering designs and processes meet nuclear regulatory, DOE, safety, and BWXT quality requirements.
• Embed compliance gates, audit readiness, and pre‑release checks throughout development.
Program Controls & Schedule
• Partner with Business Operations and Program Controls to maintain a resource‑loaded critical path schedule.
• Support earned value management (EVM) discipline and weekly KPI reviews (SPI/CPI, cost variance, schedule adherence).
Supply Chain & Technical Readiness
• Define technical acceptance criteria for supplier parts, processes, tooling, and special manufacturing steps.
• Support supplier onboarding speed, delivery performance, and technical readiness to protect schedule-critical components.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work closely with CMDF (prototype/pilot operations), CMF (full-rate industrialization), the CTO/Technology organization, and Operations.
• Drive the transition from low‑rate initial production (LRIP) to full‑rate production (FRP) on cost and schedule.
Required Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (advanced degree preferred).
• Fifteen (15+) years of progressive engineering leadership in high‑precision, highly regulated manufacturing environments (nuclear, aerospace, defense, automotive, semiconductor, or similar).
• Demonstrated experience designing, building, commissioning, and scaling a high‑precision manufacturing facility to high‑volume production.
• Strong expertise in advanced manufacturing, automation, precision machining, assembly, metrology, and inspection systems.
• Must be a U.S. citizen capable of obtaining and maintaining a DOE Q clearance; active clearance preferred.
• Proven ability to lead large, multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced, highly technical environment.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience with automotive‑scale manufacturing and assembly; Lean/Six Sigma leadership.
• Hands-on experience deploying Industry 4.0, digital thread, digital twin, and smart factory systems.
• Experience guiding organizations from prototype/pilot phases to high‑rate production in startup‑like or greenfield environments.
What We Offer
• Competitive compensation and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.
• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance (as applicable).
• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs, leadership training, and support for continuing education.
• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates diverse perspectives and enables collaboration across all generations.
• The opportunity to shape a mission‑driven organization advancing the future of energy and national security.
• Continuous learning and development opportunities to support long‑term career growth.
Pay: $200,000 - $271,000
The base salary range for this position in Tennessee (US-TN) at the start of employment is expected to be between $200,000 and $271,000 per year. However, the base salary offered is based on local job market factors, and may vary further depending on factors specific to the selected job candidate, such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other objective business considerations. Subject to these considerations, the total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, such as an annual cash incentive in addition to a full range of medical, retirement, and/or other benefits. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided at such time the selected job candidate receives an offer of employment. If hired, the selected job candidate will be employed 'at-will,’ unless employed at a location and in a position subject to a collective bargaining agreement. The company further reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment, compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, company or individual department/team performance, and other market factors.
As a federal government contractor, BWX Technologies, Inc. and any subsidiaries, affiliates and related entities (“BWXT” or the “Company”) complies with all federal, state, and local laws and customer requirements regarding health and safety protocols. As such, all BWXT new hires will be required to adhere to applicable Company health and safety requirements within the workplace as a condition of employment.
All candidates must be U.S. citizens. Selected applicants are required to successfully complete a pre-employment check and drug screening.
